head:
Executive Orbe*,.
Schedule A, Subdivision IV, paragraph 6 of the Civil Service Rules
excepting certain positions from the requirement of examination is hereby
amended to read as follows:
6. All positions on torpedo and mine planters and cable boats,
both navigating and operative, of the Quartermaster Corps of the
Army.
This amendment is recommended by the War Department and ap-
proved by the Civil Service Commission, on representations of the
Department that the same reasons exist for excepting positions on cable
boats as on torpedo and mine planters. The qualifications for employ-
ment on these vessels differ from those required in corresponding posi-
tions on other vessels, and the frequent sailing and the fact that the
vessels do not sail between fixed points render it difficult to make appoint-
ments under the civil service rules.
WOOD ROW WILSON

Miss Agnes Decry may be appointed as a nurse in the Indian Service
without reference to the requirement of examination under the civil service
rules. This action, based upon the recommendation of the Secretary of
the Interior, is in fulfillment of an agreement between representatives of
the Departments of the Interior and War in October, 1912, when it wvas
understood that Miss Deery wvas eligible for transfer.

and success in the positions of matron and nurse. The Apache prisoners
having been removed to the Mescalero Agency, New Mexico, it is desired
to appoint Miss Decry as nurse in the Indian Service.

order.

11 May, 1915.

Mr. Bernard R. Jett may be transferred in the Office of the Secre-
tary of the Interior from wireman on the per diem roll to electrician at
$1000 per annum.
Mr. Jett is employed on the "Repair of Buildings" roll in a position
for many years not regarded by the Department as classified. He was
one of a small number whose retention and reemployment without a com-
petitive status were authorized by an executive order of June 17, 1909.
He has been emnnloyed intermittently since September 9, 192 has passed
the examination for electrician, and by reason of extensive and varied
electrical work has become familiar with the complicated systems of light-
ing, being one of the fewv persons wvho wvill be able to assist materially in
the preparation of long deferred electrical plans for the several buildings.
The action proposed will also save several hundred dollars annually by
permitting the continuous employment of skilled mechanics who must
otherwise be laid off when their services cannot wvell be spared.
In view of these facts the Commission concurs with the Department
in recommending the transfer of Mr. Jett by executive order.

9 0The yea limit upon eligibility for reinstatement is hereby waived to
permit the reinstatement of Mr. Albert J. Phillips as associate chemist at
$2000 per annum in the service of the Bureau of Standards, Department
of Commerce, at Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
Mr. Phillips was in the service from August 13, 1906b, to June 15,
1913, when he resigned. He is especially recommended by the Director
of the Bureau of Standards on account of his satisfactory and efficient
service. Difficulty has been experienced in obtaining a suitably qualified
person for filling the position.
The Civil Service Commission concurs in recommending this Execu-
tive order because of Mr. Phillips long and efficient service, the compara-
tively short period of his separation from the service, and the need of an
employee with his training, which it has been difficult to meet through the
usual procedure.

forest inspector at $2800 per annum without regard to the year limit of

forestry examination on March I1, 1905, and resigned on September 30,
1910. His salary wvas increased from $iooo to $2500 per annum by suc-
